### Overview

[`dlg2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2hist)
converts a dialog into alternating user turns and AI reply strings. It
accepts a
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog) or
an iterable of messages, plus a model-capability dictionary. Each user
turn contains the prompt and any preceding notes, code, and media. Hosts
use this history as input to a model.

[`Message.hist_xml`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#message.hist_xml)
formats one message as XML.
[`Message.to_media`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#message.to_media)
collects its media.
[`Message.to_parts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#message.to_parts)
combines both into the list of text and media items for history.

For structured chat messages, use
[`dlg2chat`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2chat).
It recovers tool calls and results from the stored replies.
[`chat2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#chat2dlg)
converts those messages back into a dialog. To edit the contents of a
single reply, use
[`reply2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#reply2dlg)
and
[`dlg2reply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2reply).

### jwrap

``` python
def jwrap(
    txts:list=['']

```

*Wrap plain `txt` in a minimal Jupyter-style cell output*

``` python
def mk(msg_type: str, content=None, output='', id=None, attachments=None):
    "Create a dummy message with output in the format for its type."
    if msg_type==scode: output = jwrap(output)
    if msg_type==sprompt: output = prompt_output(output)
    res = Message(msg_type=msg_type, output=output, id=id, attachments=attachments)
    res.content = content or f'{msg_type}>{res.id}'
    res.dlg = dlg
    return res
```

## Media

A model needs both the media and enough context to identify it. We put
an XML `<media>` tag immediately before each media item. The tag records
its `id`, `type`, and `mime`.

The ID identifies the source:

- An attachment uses its UUID from the Markdown `attachment:uuid`
  reference.
- A variable uses its name.
- A code output image uses a content hash.

The `type` attribute describes where the media came from. `output` means
a code cell output. `variable` means a variable value. `content` means
media embedded in the message’s Markdown.

### Media context tags

[`media_item`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#media_item)
accepts bytes, a
[`MediaUrl`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#mediaurl),
or a function that loads either. It checks the MIME type against the
model’s capabilities before preparing the data. Successful results
contain the `<media>` tag followed by the data.

The capability flags are `supports_vision`, `supports_video_input`,
`supports_pdf_input`, and `supports_audio_input`. A missing flag means
no support for that media type. The unsupported-media message asks the
user to choose a model that supports it.

Expected failures return a `<media-unavailable>` tag. These include
missing files, invalid base64, and unavailable or unsupported data. The
tag records the reason and tells the model to inform the user that it
cannot see the media. Image preparation and a host’s path checks can
also report these failures. Unexpected exceptions still propagate.

PDF token estimates use a page count.
[`pdf_pages`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#pdf_pages)
reads `/Count` values from `/Pages` nodes without a PDF library. In a
complete page tree, the root holds the total and no child has a larger
count. The function takes the largest count it finds.

PDF 1.5 permits these nodes inside compressed object streams.
[`pdf_pages`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#pdf_pages)
uses `zlib` to inspect those streams too. An incremental edit that
removes pages can leave an older, larger root in the file. Counting that
root overestimates the token budget rather than underestimating it. This
is a heuristic, not a complete PDF parser. It returns zero when it finds
no matching count.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L119"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### pdf_pages

``` python
def pdf_pages(
    b:bytes
):
```

*Page count of PDF `b`: the largest `/Count` on a `/Pages` node, in the
clear or inside an inflated object stream*

These hand-built PDFs contain the same page tree, once uncompressed and
once in a compressed object stream:

``` python
def _pdf(objs): return b'%PDF-1.5\n' + b''.join(f'{i} 0 obj\n'.encode()+o+b'\nendobj\n' for i,o in enumerate(objs, 1)) + b'%%EOF'
pages = b'<< /Type /Pages /Count 3 /Kids [3 0 R 4 0 R 5 0 R] >>'
kids = [b'<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R >>']*3
plain = _pdf([b'<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>', pages, *kids])
packed = zlib.compress(b'2 0 ' + pages)
objstm = _pdf([b'<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>', b'<< /Type /ObjStm /N 1 /First 4 /Filter /FlateDecode /Length %d >>\nstream\n' % len(packed) + packed + b'\nendstream', *kids])
test_eq((pdf_pages(plain), pdf_pages(objstm), pdf_pages(b'%PDF-1.5\n%%EOF')), (3, 3, 0))
pdf_pages(objstm)
```

    3

Use
[`output_parts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#output_parts)
when a host needs to send code output images to a model. Solveit uses it
for tool results. The same function can prepare media for an MCP
frontend. It checks model support, resizes images, and adds their ID
tags. It returns
[`Part`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#part)
objects, including unavailable-media notices for expected failures.
Images are enabled when `aim_info` is `None`.

[`merge_media`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#merge_media)
combines these parts with the rendered output text. If the parts include
an image, it returns a list. Each media tag stays next to its image,
with the output text last. Without an image, it returns a plain string
containing the output text followed by any unavailable-media notices.
Callers use this return type to distinguish text-only results from
multipart results.

### Static media refs

Add `#ai` to a Markdown image target to include it in model context:
`![alt](ref#ai)`. The model doesn’t see media from links without this
suffix.

The target can be an `http://` or `https://` URL, a `data:` URL, or a
file path. Web URLs use a lazy
[`MediaUrl`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#mediaurl).
Data URLs decode inline.
[`Dialog.media_path`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dialog.media_path)
resolves file paths.

Hosts patch `media_path` to apply their own directories and safety
rules. Solveit uses it to map `/static/` and restrict production access
to its data directory.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L168"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Dialog.media_path

``` python
def media_path(
    ref
):
```

*Resolve a file reference to an absolute path. Hosts can override path
and safety rules.*

By default, `media_path` resolves relative paths against the dialog’s
directory.
[`create_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#create_dlg)
and
[`read_ipynb`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/ipynb.html#read_ipynb)
record that location in `path_`. Absolute paths don’t need a dialog
directory. The result of either lookup is a resolved absolute path:

``` python
tdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()
(tdir/'sq.png').write_bytes(png)
stdlg = Dialog(name='statics')
stdlg.path_ = str(tdir/'statics.ipynb')
test_eq(stdlg.media_path('sq.png'), tdir/'sq.png')
test_eq(stdlg.media_path('/abs/x.png'), Path('/abs/x.png'))
```

[`_media_static`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#_media_static)
keeps the order of the tagged links. Local files and data URLs produce
tags followed by bytes. Raster images pass through `prep_img`. Web URLs
produce tags followed by lazy
[`MediaUrl`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#mediaurl)
objects. An unreadable file produces an unavailable-media tag. Untagged
links contribute nothing:

``` python
m = Message('some text', dlg=stdlg)
test_eq(_media_static(m, {}), [])
m = Message('a ![](sq.png#ai), a skipped ![](sq.png), and ![](https://ex.org/logo.png#ai)', dlg=stdlg)
res = _media_static(m, dict(supports_vision=True))
test_eq(len(res), 4)
test_eq(res[0], '<media id="sq.png" type="content" mime="image/png"></media>')
test(res[1], bytes, isinstance)
test_eq(res[2], '<media id="https://ex.org/logo.png" type="content" mime="image/png"></media>')
test(res[3], MediaUrl, isinstance)
```

``` python
m = Message('A tiny square ![Square](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAoAAAAKCAIAAAACUFjqAAAAE0lEQVR4nGP8z4APMOGVZRip0gBBLAETee26JgAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==#ai) and a bad ref ![](nope.png#ai)', dlg=stdlg)
res = _media_static(m, dict(supports_vision=True))
test_eq(len(res), 3)
test_eq(res[0], '<media id="iVBORw0KGg" type="content" mime="image/png"></media>')
test(res[1], bytes, isinstance)
test(res[2], '<media-unavailable', operator.contains)
```

### The [`mk_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#mk_msgs) contract

Hosts pass the history from this module to
[`aidialog.msg_parts.mk_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#mk_msgs).
The nesting of its lists determines which items belong to the same turn.
A flat list alternates user and assistant turns:

``` python
from aidialog.msg_parts import mk_msgs, mk_msg
from fastcore import imghdr
```

``` python
mk_msgs(['hello', "here's a response"])
```

    [Msg(role='user', content=[Text(raw=None, cache_control=None, text='hello', citations=None)], raw=None),
     Msg(role='assistant', content=[Text(raw=None, cache_control=None, text="here's a response", citations=None)], raw=None)]

A nested list groups parts within one turn. Here the user sends three
text parts before the assistant responds:

``` python
mk_msgs([['hello1', 'hello2', 'hello3'], "here's a response"])
```

    [Msg(role='user', content=[Text(raw=None, cache_control=None, text='hello1', citations=None), Text(raw=None, cache_control=None, text='hello2', citations=None), Text(raw=None, cache_control=None, text='hello3', citations=None)], raw=None),
     Msg(role='assistant', content=[Text(raw=None, cache_control=None, text="here's a response", citations=None)], raw=None)]

Inside a turn,
[`mk_content`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#mk_content)
converts recognized image bytes to an image part. It checks their MIME
type with `detect_mime`, which uses `imghdr.what` for images. This
handles the bytes that follow each `<media>` tag:

``` python
test_eq(imghdr.what(None, b'not an image'), None)
test_eq(imghdr.what(None, png), 'png')
mk_msg(['hello', png, 'hello3'])
```

- role: `user`

<contents>

hello

## Sigil refs and variables

Prompts can refer to kernel values, tools, and shell output with a
character before a backtick expression:

- $\`expr\` requests the value of a kernel expression.
- &\`tool\` activates a tool.
- !\`cmd\` requests shell output in hosts that provide a shell.

This module parses the references. The host evaluates them because it
owns the kernel, toolset, and shell.

[`get_refs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#get_refs)
parses names for the `&` form. It accepts a single name or a list such
as &\`\[python, bash\]\`.
[`sigil_pat`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#sigil_pat)
handles `$` and `!`. Their backtick content can be an expression or
command, rather than a name.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L191"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### get_refs

``` python
def get_refs(
    cts, sigil:str='&'
):
```

*Return sorted unique names referenced via sigil`name` or
sigil`[name, name]` pattern in msgs*

``` python
test_eq(get_refs('use &`bash` and &`[python, bash]`'), ['bash', 'python'])
test_eq(get_refs('dotted names too: &`np.load`'), ['np.load'])
test_is(get_refs('no refs here, and no $`vars` either'), None)
```

[`get_exprs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#get_exprs)
collects references from prompt content. `expr_mtypes` defines the
participating message types. Notes, code, and outputs don’t request
interpolation, even when they contain the same syntax. Pass `sigil='!'`
to collect shell references instead of kernel expressions. Parsing
doesn’t evaluate either kind of reference.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L204"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### get_exprs

``` python
def get_exprs(
    msgs, sigil:str='$'

```

*Sorted unique refs of `sigil` form found in prompt messages of `msgs`*

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### sigil_pat

``` python
def sigil_pat(
    sigil

```

*Regex for sigil`payload` refs, e.g. $`expr` or !`cmd`*

``` python
test_eq(expr_pat.findall('$`myvar`'), ['myvar'])
test_eq(expr_pat.findall('$`now()`'), ['now()'])
test_eq(expr_pat.findall('$`add(1, 2)`'), ['add(1, 2)'])
test_eq(expr_pat.findall('$`[obj.attr, d["key"], fn(*args,**kws)]`'), ['[obj.attr, d["key"], fn(*args,**kws)]'])
test_eq(expr_pat.findall('Check $`x` and $`f(y)`'), ['x', 'f(y)'])
```

References in notes and code stay out of the result. Repeating a
reference in prompts adds no duplicate:

``` python
raw = [mk('prompt', '>hello $`x`'), mk('note', '$`not_variable1`'), mk('code', output="aaa", content="'$`not_variable2`'"),
    mk('prompt', 'hi <hi $`y`'), mk('prompt', '$`x`, $`y`')]
test_eq(get_exprs(raw), ['x', 'y'])
raw += [mk('prompt', 'run !`ls -la` and !`git status`'), mk('note', '!`not_a_cmd`')]
test_eq(get_exprs(raw, sigil='!'), ['git status', 'ls -la'])
test_eq(get_exprs(raw), ['x', 'y'])  # the default is unaffected by ! refs
```

After evaluation, the host supplies a dictionary mapping each reference
to its value.
[`vars_tag`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#vars_tag)
prepares those values for context. Ordinary values go in a `<variables>`
element made with fastcore’s `Variables` and `Variable` components.
Recognized media values go in separate media parts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L211"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### vars_tag

``` python
def vars_tag(
    aim_info, ns:NoneType=None
):
```

*<Variables> element and byte variables for this message*

``` python
imns = dict(img=_mk_img(_imgb64), x=4, y=3, img2=_mk_img(_imgb64))
vt = vars_tag(dict(supports_vision=True), imns)
test_eq(to_xml(vt['vars_tag']), '''<variables>The 'variables' section provides values of: $`img`, $`x`, $`y`, $`img2`<variable name="x" type="int">4</variable><variable name="y" type="int">3</variable></variables>''')
```

Media variables use alternating tags and bytes. Images, audio, and video
can all go in a
[`mk_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#mk_msgs)
content list this way:

``` python
test_eq(len(vt['vars_bytes']), 4)
test_eq(vt['vars_bytes'][0], '<media id="img" type="variable" mime="image/png"></media>')
test_eq(vt['vars_bytes'][2], '<media id="img2" type="variable" mime="image/png"></media>')
```

Shell results use the full !\`cmd\` reference as their variable name.
[`vars_tag`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#vars_tag)
keeps that spelling in the introductory text and the variable tag. Shell
results share the same section and position as other variables:

``` python
vt = vars_tag({}, {'x': 4, '!`ls -la`': 'total 0'})
test_eq(to_xml(vt['vars_tag']), '''<variables>The 'variables' section provides values of: $`x`, !`ls -la`<variable name="x" type="int">4</variable><variable name="!`ls -la`" type="str">total 0</variable></variables>''')
```

[`vars_hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#vars_hist)
returns one user turn containing the namespace and an assistant
acknowledgement. Hosts prepend this exchange to history. Variable values
then appear once at a stable position for caching. An empty namespace
produces no exchange:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L223"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### vars_hist

``` python
def vars_hist(
    aim_info, ns:NoneType=None
):
```

*Single history turn holding all variable values, to sit above
everything else*

``` python
test_eq(vars_hist({}, {}), [])
test_eq(vars_hist({}, None), [])
vh = vars_hist({}, {'x': 4, 'y': 3})
test_eq(len(vh), 2)
test_eq(vh[0][0], """<variables>The 'variables' section provides values of: $`x`, $`y`<variable name="x" type="int">4</variable><variable name="y" type="int">3</variable></variables>""")
vh = vars_hist(dict(supports_vision=True), {'img': _mk_img(_imgb64), 'x': 4})
test_eq(len(vh[0]), 3)
test_eq(vh[0][1], '<media id="img" type="variable" mime="image/png"></media>')
```

Hosts evaluate references in their kernels with ipyfuncs’ `eval_exprs`,
usually through a client helper. Each requested expression has a result.
Evaluation failures return an `<error>` element as a string instead of
omitting the key. Its `type` attribute identifies the exception.

[`is_nameerr`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#is_nameerr)
recognizes the `NameError` marker. Hosts use it to warn about missing
variables rather than show the error as a variable value. Other errors
remain visible in the values. This distinguishes a missing name from a
reference whose evaluation failed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L234"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### is_nameerr

``` python
def is_nameerr(
    v
):
```

*Does an `eval_exprs` result mark an undefined name?*

## Message XML Helpers

[`Message.hist_xml`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#message.hist_xml)
formats notes, code, and other non-prompt messages with `item2xml`. The
tag names the message type and contains the content directly. An `<out>`
section contains any output. This history rendering includes time
information.
[`Message.to_xml`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.to_xml)
provides the concise rendering used by dlgskill.

Prompts use `prompt_txt` instead. The AI reply belongs to the next
history turn, not inside the prompt XML.

### The prompt envelope

A user turn can contain notes, code, and media before the prompt.
[`task_tags`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#task_tags)
separates the actual request from that context. It returns an
`<instructions>` element followed by a `<prompt>` element containing the
request.

The prompt’s `sid` identifies the message for tools. Its `time` records
the local run time when available. `prompt_txt` uses the dialog’s
timezone, or UTC without one.

Hosts can add warnings alongside the live prompt.
[`warning_tag`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#warning_tag)
puts these in a `<system-reminder>` element. Examples include undefined
variables and context-budget trims.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L245"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### warning_tag

``` python
def warning_tag(
    warning:str
):
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L239"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### task_tags

``` python
def task_tags(
    task:str, sid:NoneType=None, time:NoneType=None, tz:str='UTC'
):
```

*Envelope elements for a prompt: `<instructions>` plus `<prompt>`
carrying `sid` and local run time*

``` python
test_eq(to_xml(task_tags("do it.", "testsid")), '<instructions>Respond to the request in the `prompt` below.</instructions><prompt sid="testsid">do it.</prompt>')
test_eq(to_xml(warning_tag('The following vars are undefined: `foo`')), '<system-reminder>**NB**: The following vars are undefined: `foo`</system-reminder>')
test_is(warning_tag(''), None)
```

`hist_xml` delegates prompt rendering to `prompt_txt`. Hosts can patch
that method without changing the other message types.
[`dlg2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2hist)
passes `last=True` for the final prompt. The default renderer uses the
same envelope for every prompt.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L256"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python

    last:bool=False
):
```

*Render message XML for history, including time information.*

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L249"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.prompt_txt

``` python
def prompt_txt(
    last:bool=False
):
```

*Render the prompt envelope. `last` does not change the default
rendering.*

``` python
# Combines content and output into full XML representation
m = mk('code', 'print("hi")', 'hi\n')
test_eq(m.hist_xml(), f'<code id="{m.id}">print("hi")<out>hi\n</out></code>')
n = mk('note', '# hey')
test_eq(n.hist_xml(), f'<markdown id="{n.id}"># hey</markdown>')  # notes render as markdown; no out, no extra tags
m.meta = dict(nbdev=dict(export='true', default_exp='core'))
test_eq(m.hist_xml(), f'<code id="{m.id}" export default_exp="core">print("hi")<out>hi\n</out></code>')  # meta directives as attrs
```

``` python
# Prompts render enveloped: instructions plus a prompt tag carrying the message id
m = mk('prompt', 'question', id='_t1')
test_eq(m.hist_xml(), '<instructions>Respond to the request in the `prompt` below.</instructions>\n<prompt sid="_t1">question</prompt>')
test_eq(m.prompt_txt(last=True), m.hist_xml())
```

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*Collect media from `#ai` Markdown links. Hosts can override this to add

``` python
# No media for plain messages
test_eq(mk('note', 'hello').to_media({}), [])
```

``` python
# Code output images
m = Message(msg_type='code', output=mk_code_output({'image/png': base64.b64encode(png).decode()}))
media = m.to_media(dict(supports_vision=True))
test_eq(len(media), 2)  # xml tag, bytes
```

`to_media` collects attachments first, then `media_extra`, then code
output images. By default, `media_extra` supplies the `#ai` links. Hosts
can patch it to add more sources. Each message keeps its own media when
`to_parts` builds history in dialog order:

``` python
m = Message('a static ![](sq.png#ai)', dlg=stdlg)
media = m.to_media(dict(supports_vision=True))
test_eq(len(media), 2)
test_eq(media[0], '<media id="sq.png" type="content" mime="image/png"></media>')
```

## Dialogs to canonical messages

[`dlg2chat`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2chat)
converts a dialog into the canonical
[`Msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#msg)
format used for provider conversions and transcript editing. It first
calls
[`dlg2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2hist)
to group the user turns.
[`reply2chat`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#reply2chat)
then parses each stored reply with `msg_parts.fmt2hist` and separates
its tool calls and results. You can also use
[`reply2chat`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#reply2chat)
on a single reply string.

The dialog must end with a prompt.
[`dlg2chat`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2chat)
rejects duplicate tool-call IDs, including duplicates in hand-authored
replies. By default, prompts include the solveit serving envelope from
[`task_tags`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#task_tags).
For transcript reconstruction, pass `plain=True` to keep the prompt’s
bare content.

This conversion does not preserve every part of a stored reply.
[`fmt2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#fmt2hist)
removes thinking blocks.
[`reply2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#reply2dlg)
and
[`dlg2reply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2reply)
have the same limitation. Keep the original reply string if you need
those blocks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L325"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### reply2chat

``` python
def reply2chat(
    outp:str
)->list[aidialog.msg_parts.Msg]:
```

*Chat messages for a stored reply:
[`fmt2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#fmt2hist)-parsed
parts in strict call/result alternation*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L330"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### dlg2chat

``` python
def dlg2chat(
    dlg, # A `Dialog`, ending with a prompt
    aim_info:NoneType=None, # Model capability dict for media handling; images enabled if None
    plain:bool=False, # Render prompts as bare content, without the serving envelope?
):
```

*Canonical chat messages for `dlg`, with each reply’s tool calls
recovered as real parts*

We’ll build a reply containing a tool-call details block in the stored
reply format:

``` python
def _mk_dtl(func, args, result, tid='x1'):
    d = json.dumps(dict(id=tid, name=func, args=args, result=result))
    return f"```json {{.tool}}\n{d}\n```"

py_dtl = _mk_dtl('python', {'code':'1+1'}, '2')
```

``` python
ddlg = Dialog(name='canon')
ddlg.mk_message('What is 1+1?', msg_type=sprompt, output=f"Check:\n\n{py_dtl}\n\nIt is 2.")
cm = dlg2chat(ddlg)
test_eq([m.role for m in cm], ['user', 'assistant', 'tool', 'assistant'])
test_eq(cm[1].content[1].name, 'python')
```

A reply can contain sequential tool calls, each using the previous
result.
[`fmt2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#fmt2hist)
groups these into an assistant message and a tool-result message.
[`dlg2chat`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2chat)
separates them again into call/result pairs in order. This matches the
sequence that live sessions record without presenting the calls as
parallel:

``` python
py_dtl2 = _mk_dtl('python', {'code':'2+2'}, '4', 'x2')
sdlg = Dialog(name='seq')
sdlg.mk_message('Two steps.', msg_type=sprompt, output=f"{py_dtl}\n\n{py_dtl2}\n\nDone.")
sm = dlg2chat(sdlg)
test_eq([(m.role, len(m.content)) for m in sm], [('user',1), ('assistant',1), ('tool',1), ('assistant',1), ('tool',1), ('assistant',1)])
test_eq(sm[2].content[0].id, sm[1].content[0].id)
test_eq(sm[4].content[0].id, sm[3].content[0].id)
```

``` python
bad = Dialog(name='dup')
bad.mk_message('a', msg_type=sprompt, output=py_dtl)
bad.mk_message('b', msg_type=sprompt, output=py_dtl)
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'duplicate tool call id'): dlg2chat(bad)
```

[`chat2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#chat2dlg)
creates one prompt per user turn. It renders the assistant and tool
messages into that prompt’s reply with
[`hist2fmt`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#hist2fmt).
User images become attachments with references in the question text.

[`hist2fmt`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#hist2fmt)
writes tool calls and results as fenced JSON. The round-trip checks
below compare canonical messages rather than the original Markdown. Its
`mx` limit truncates tool results and permits string arguments up to
five times that length. Use `mx=None` to disable these limits for
matched call/result pairs. Server calls without separate results still
use their default display limit.

[`chat2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#chat2dlg)
removes the prompt envelope and keeps the request text. An envelope’s
`sid` restores the original message ID. Converting the reconstructed
dialog back to chat then restores that ID in the envelope.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L347"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### chat2dlg

``` python
def chat2dlg(
    msgs, # Canonical messages, e.g. from `dlg2chat`
    name, # Dialog name
    cls:type=Dialog, # Dialog class to create
    mx:int=2000, # Maximum characters per rendered tool input/output string; None disables truncation (see `hist2fmt`)
):
```

*Convert canonical messages to a dialog with one prompt per user turn.*

``` python
rdlg = chat2dlg(dlg2chat(sdlg), 'seq round-trip')
test_eq(len(rdlg.messages), 1)
test_eq(rdlg.messages[0].content, 'Two steps.')
test_eq(dlg2chat(rdlg), sm)
```

Producers can attach provenance to a
[`Msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#msg) with
a dynamic `meta` attribute. It isn’t a class field. For example,
`recs2chat` and `items2chat` record the source’s `created` time and
`uid` there.

[`chat2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#chat2dlg)
copies each user message’s metadata to its dialog message. It derives an
eight-hex-digit ID from the `uid`. Repeating the conversion preserves
these IDs and the link to the source record. An embedded solveit `sid`
takes precedence:

``` python
mm = mk_msg('When was this?')
mm.meta = dict(created='2026-07-09T00:26:40.000Z', uid='abc-123')
mdlg = chat2dlg([mm, Msg('assistant', [Text('July 9.')])], 'meta')
m0 = mdlg.messages[0]
test_eq(m0.meta, mm.meta)
test_eq(m0.id, hashlib.md5(b'abc-123').hexdigest()[:8])
m0.meta
```

    {'created': '2026-07-09T00:26:40.000Z', 'uid': 'abc-123'}

Without a provenance `uid`,
[`chat2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#chat2dlg)
derives the ID from the dialog name and turn position. Repeating the
conversion with the same name and turns gives the same IDs:

``` python
d1,d2 = chat2dlg([mk_msg('a'), Msg('assistant', [Text('b')])], 'same'), chat2dlg([mk_msg('a'), Msg('assistant', [Text('b')])], 'same')
test_eq(d1.messages[0].id, d2.messages[0].id)
```

A continuation transcript can start with assistant messages when earlier
turns are in a predecessor file.
[`chat2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#chat2dlg)
puts these replies on an empty first prompt instead of raising an error:

``` python
fdlg = chat2dlg([Msg('assistant', [Text('...continuing.')]), mk_msg('And then?'), Msg('assistant', [Text('Done.')])], 'cont')
test_eq(len(fdlg.messages), 2)
test_eq(fdlg.messages[0].content, '')
assert '...continuing.' in fdlg.messages[0].ai_res
fdlg.summary()
```

    ba0dfd85:p:
    > ...continuing.
    753e7837:p:And then?
    > Done.

Notes and code before a prompt join that prompt’s user turn. This dialog
shows prompts with and without preceding context, plus an empty AI
response. The image questions are plain text here; the media examples
above show how to attach the images themselves:

``` python
raw = [
    mk('prompt', 'hello there', output='Hello! How can I help?'),
    mk('note', 'a note between turns'),
    mk('code', output="aaa", content="'some source text'"),
    mk('prompt', 'add the numbers', output='They sum to 4.'),
    mk('note'), 
    mk('note'), 
    mk('code', output="333"),
    mk('prompt'),  # empty output on purpose
    mk('prompt', 'summarize the conversation so far', output='We greeted, then added some numbers.'),
    mk('note', 'below we insert an image'),
    mk('code', 'img=..some code to read image bytes'),
    mk('prompt', 'Please tell me what you see in the image', output='I can see...'),
    mk('note', 'lets add an image note'),
    mk('prompt', 'Please tell me what you see in the 2 images in the above msg',output='i see two puppies!'),
    mk('prompt', 'And one final question.')]
```

``` python
aim_info = dict(supports_vision=True)
```

``` python
*hist,p,_ = dlg2hist(raw, aim_info)
```

Let’s take a look at the history:

``` python
for idx, turn in enumerate(hist):
    display(Markdown(f"**======turn: {idx}======**"))
    display(turn)
```

Codecs can retain session records as raw messages with a `rec_kind`
metadata tag. One example is a system record from `llmsurgery.ant`.
These records support reconstruction of the session file.
[`dlg2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2hist)
excludes them from model context:

``` python
tr = [mk('note', 'context'), mk('prompt', 'q', output='r')]
h1 = dlg2hist(tr, aim_info)
trd = Dialog(name='trd'); trd.messages = list(tr)
test_eq(dlg2hist(trd, aim_info), h1)  # a Dialog and its message list produce the same history
tr.insert(1, Message('', msg_type=sraw, meta=dict(rec_kind='system', rec=dict(type='system'))))
test_eq(dlg2hist(tr, aim_info), h1)  # tagged raws never leak into history
```

[`dlg2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2hist)
also excludes messages with `skipped` set. They remain in the dialog for
display and saving. Clearing `skipped` restores them to history. The
`pinned` flag has no effect here. Hosts use it to protect messages from
eviction.

``` python
sk = [mk('note', 'context'), mk('code', 'x = 1', output='1'), mk('prompt', 'q', output='r')]
full = dlg2hist(sk, aim_info)
sk[1].skipped = 1
h = dlg2hist(sk, aim_info)
test_eq(h, dlg2hist([sk[0], sk[2]], aim_info))   # projects as if the skipped message weren't there
assert h != full
sk[1].skipped = 0
test_eq(dlg2hist(sk, aim_info), full)            # unskip restores it
```

``` python
# test each user input for expected length
test_eq(len(hist[0]),1) # prompt w/o preceding msgs
test_eq(len(hist[2]),3) # prompt w preceding note and code
test_eq(len(hist[4]),4) # prompt w preceding notes (2) and code
test_eq(len(hist[6]),1) # prompt w/o preceding msgs
test_eq(len(hist[8]),3)  # [note, code, prompt]
test_eq(len(hist[10]),2)  # [note, prompt]
```

``` python
# Test each AI output for expected length
for i in (1,3,7,9,11): test(len(hist[i]),0,operator.gt)
test_eq(hist[5],'<output result="pending" reason="incomplete"/>')  # empty ai response
```

## Reply sub-dialogs

A prompt stores its AI reply as Markdown with fenced JSON tool blocks.
Convert legacy HTML details blocks with
[`conv_tools`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#conv_tools)
before parsing them. Use
[`reply2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#reply2dlg)
to turn a reply into a dialog of notes and code messages. You can then
edit it with the usual message operations.
[`dlg2reply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2reply)
converts the edited dialog back to reply Markdown.

[`reply2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#reply2dlg)
parses through
[`fmt2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#fmt2hist).
That parser removes token-usage and thinking blocks. When the reply ends
with tool results, it adds a final `.` note to avoid empty assistant
text. These changes also occur when converting replies to chat history.

[`fmt2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#fmt2hist)
retains server-tool calls.
[`reply2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#reply2dlg)
converts them to code messages too, but the sub-dialog does not retain
their `server` flag.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L380"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### reply2dlg

``` python
def reply2dlg(
    pmsg
):
```

*Explode `pmsg`’s AI reply into a
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog) of
note and code messages*

[`reply2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#reply2dlg)
writes each tool call as Python source with `repr` values for the
keyword arguments. The source is the sole record of the tool name and
arguments. Later, `ast` parses them back without executing the call. The
output list holds the result. The message’s `meta['tool_id']` holds the
call ID.

Here’s a reply containing prose, a Python tool call, and its result.
We’ll turn it into a sub-dialog, edit the call’s argument, and convert
it back:

``` python
tu1 = ToolUse(id='x1', name='python', arguments={'code':'1+1'})
tr1 = ToolResult(id='x1', name='python', text='2')
rmsgs = [Msg(role='assistant', content=[Text('Check:'), tu1]), Msg(role='tool', content=[tr1]),
    Msg(role='assistant', content=[Text('It is 2.')])]
pm = Message('What is 1+1?', msg_type=sprompt, output=hist2fmt(rmsgs, mx=None))
Markdown(pm.ai_res)
```

Check:

``` json
{
  "id": "x1",
  "name": "python",
  "args": {
    "code": "1+1"
  },
  "result": "2"
}
```

It is 2.

``` python
sub = reply2dlg(pm)
sub
```

**4340d65d**

<details>

- Check:
- python(code=‘1+1’) ⇒ \[{‘output_type’: ‘execute_result’, ‘metadata’:
  {}, ‘data’: …
- It is 2.

</details>

``` python
test_eq([m.msg_type for m in sub.messages], [snote, scode, snote])
test_eq(sub.messages[1].content, "python(code='1+1')")
test_eq(sub.messages[1].output, code_output('2'))
test_eq(sub.messages[1].meta['tool_id'], 'x1')
sub.messages[1]
```

8a814699:c:python(code=‘1+1’) ⇒ out(102)

Dotted tool names such as `tools.write_stdin` remain valid Python calls.
The resulting code message can run in an environment that provides the
tool:

``` python
dtc = ToolUse('d1', 'tools.write_stdin', {'session_id':7, 'chars':'x'})
dpm = Message('Continue.', msg_type=sprompt, output=hist2fmt(
    [Msg(role='assistant', content=[dtc]), mk_tool_res_msg([dtc], ['ok']), Msg(role='assistant', content=[Text('Done.')])], mx=None))
dsub = reply2dlg(dpm)
test_eq(dsub.messages[0].content, "tools.write_stdin(session_id=7, chars='x')")
dsub.messages[0].content
```

    "tools.write_stdin(session_id=7, chars='x')"

[`dlg2reply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2reply)
converts code messages to fenced JSON tool blocks with
[`mk_tr_details`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#mk_tr_details),
without truncation. Each block records the call ID, name, arguments, and
result. Notes keep their text apart from surrounding whitespace. The
function joins the nonempty blocks with blank lines.

For replies already in the normalized
[`hist2fmt`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#hist2fmt)
format, these examples round-trip exactly:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L413"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### dlg2reply

``` python
def dlg2reply(
    sub
):
```

*Implode a sub-dialog of note and code messages back into reply
markdown*

``` python
test_eq(dlg2reply(sub), pm.ai_res)
test_eq(dlg2reply(dsub), dpm.ai_res)
```

Changing a keyword argument in the source changes that argument in the
reply. The call keeps its ID:

``` python
sub.messages[1].content = "python(code='1+2')"
tu = first(p for m in fmt2hist(dlg2reply(sub)) for p in m.content if isinstance(p, ToolUse))
test_eq(tu.arguments, {'code':'1+2'})
test_eq(tu.id, 'x1')
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/hist.py#L420"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.tool_call

``` python
def tool_call():
```

*Parsed `dict(name=..., arguments=...)` when this code message’s source
is a literal tool call, else None*

For UIs and review code, `tool_call` reads the name and arguments
without generating an ID or changing the message. It returns `None` for
a note or source that isn’t a keyword-only call expression. Argument
values must be Python literals. Nonliteral values raise during parsing:

``` python
test_eq(sub.messages[1].tool_call, dict(name='python', arguments={'code':'1+2'}))
test_eq(sub.messages[0].tool_call, None)  # a note
test_eq(Message('x = 1', msg_type=scode).tool_call, None)  # not a call expression
```

Parallel tool calls appear as adjacent tool blocks in a stored reply.
[`reply2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#reply2dlg)
makes one code message per call in document order. The final `.` note
comes from
[`fmt2hist`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#fmt2hist).
Converting this reply to a sub-dialog and back preserves the history
from
[`dlg2chat`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2chat):

``` python
tus = [ToolUse(id=f'x{i}', name='simple_add', arguments=dict(a=i, b=1)) for i in (2,3,4)]
tres = [ToolResult(id=f'x{i}', name='simple_add', text=str(i+1)) for i in (2,3,4)]
vmsgs = [Msg(role='assistant', content=[Text('Adding.'), *tus]), Msg(role='tool', content=tres)]
vdlg = Dialog(name='volley')
vpm = vdlg.mk_message('Add some numbers.', msg_type=sprompt, output=hist2fmt(vmsgs, mx=None))
vsub = reply2dlg(vpm)
test_eq([m.msg_type for m in vsub.messages], [snote, scode, scode, scode, snote])
```

``` python
v2 = Dialog(name='volley2')
v2.mk_message('Add some numbers.', msg_type=sprompt, output=dlg2reply(vsub), id=vpm.id)
test_eq(dlg2chat(v2), dlg2chat(vdlg))
```

You can insert new notes and calls into the sub-dialog.
[`dlg2reply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2reply)
includes them in the reply and assigns IDs to calls that don’t have one.
The example checks that the IDs are distinct:

``` python
vsub.mk_message('One more:', msg_type=snote)
nc = vsub.mk_message('simple_add(a=5, b=1)', output=code_output('6'))
r3 = dlg2reply(vsub)
assert 'One more:' in r3
ids = [p.id for m in fmt2hist(r3) for p in m.content if isinstance(p, ToolUse)]
test_eq(len(ids), len(set(ids)))
assert nc.meta['tool_id']
```

A reply without tool calls becomes one note.
[`reply2dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#reply2dlg)
raises `ValueError` for a tool name that isn’t a dotted Python
identifier.
[`dlg2reply`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/hist.html#dlg2reply)
raises for code that isn’t a keyword-only tool call:

``` python
sub1 = reply2dlg(Message('hi', msg_type=sprompt, output='Just prose.'))
test_eq([m.msg_type for m in sub1.messages], [snote])
test_eq(dlg2reply(sub1), 'Just prose.')
```

``` python
badp = [Msg(role='assistant', content=[ToolUse(id='b1', name='foo-bar')]),
    Msg(role='tool', content=[ToolResult(id='b1', name='foo-bar', text='x')])]
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'identifier'): reply2dlg(Message('p', msg_type=sprompt, output=hist2fmt(badp, mx=None)))
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'tool call'): dlg2reply(Dialog(name='b', messages=[Message('1+1', msg_type=scode)]))
```
